VBO:0201107.summary: Lively, vocal and ready for action, the Pumi brings a terrier-like style to Hungarian herding work. Its standard describes boldness and some reserve toward strangers. The fawn form shares that working character with the other colors; the breed also has a documented scenting role in tackling rodents and larger animals.
VBO:0201107.shortDescription: A lively, vocal Hungarian herder; the fawn form shares the breed’s bold working character and scenting skills.

sources.title: Pumi: Official FCI Breed Standard
sources.evidence: The official standard describes lively/noisy, bold herding temperament with reserve toward strangers, herding larger livestock and well-developed scenting/rodent work. GeneralAppearance and detailed morphology define square proportions, tipped ears, coat and full circular tail. Color names fawnFako red/yellow/cream with dark shading; behavior is shared breed-standard tendency, not color-specific empirical research.

sources.title: Pumi: Official FCI Nomenclature and Varieties
sources.evidence: Explicitly recognizes fawnFako, primarycolorsred/yellow/cream as Pumi coatvariety.

VBO:0201092.summary: Happy, lively and even-tempered in its breed standard, the Pug is a companion dog whose appeal centers on its expressive character. Apricot is one of its recognized coat varieties, with no separate temperament assigned to the color. The breed’s history runs from China to Europe through Dutch traders, and later to England with William III.
VBO:0201092.shortDescription: A lively, even-tempered companion in the breed standard; apricot is a coat variety, with the same Pug character.
